atoms.b: Although most people living in Britain at the time were ((++Christians Muslims)), the Vikings were Pagans. This means they worshipped many gods and goddesses.
Vikings also believed that the world was made up of nine different realms. These included Midgard, home of the ((aliens ++humans)), and Asgard, home of the gods.
Odin is one of the most important Viking gods. He is the ((++king queen)) of all gods and created Midgard and Asgard.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: The same Anglo-Saxon Pagan god is called Woden.

atoms.b: Loki is the god of mischief. ((++Vikings Romans)) believed that Loki could turn into beasts, objects and even other people.
Frigg is Odin’s wife and the goddess of love, ((++motherhood mischief)) and marriage.
atoms.sound: Freegh is Odin’s wife and the goddess of love, motherhood and marriage.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: The same Anglo-Saxon Pagan goddess is called Frige.
hint.sound: The same Anglo-Saxon Pagan goddess is called Freegh.

atoms.b: Thor is the god of thunder. He fights with a mighty ((++hammer sword)) and protects Asgard, the home of the gods.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: The same Anglo-Saxon Pagan god is called Thunor.

atoms.text: The Vikings were fierce warriors who valued bravery and a “good death” in battle. If they died fighting, they believed they would be taken to Valhalla.
Valhalla is a hall in Asgard where they would become heroes and spend eternity eating, drinking and practising fighting.
Those that didn’t die bravely in battle went to Helheim instead. In one part of Helheim, evil and dishonest people were punished.
However, there were also areas of Helheim for good people who weren’t warriors. This included ordinary people like farmers or blacksmiths.

atoms.a: Where did Vikings believe they would go if they died in battle?
What would they do in Valhalla?
Who did Vikings believe would go to Helheim?

instruction.text: Decide where each of these Vikings would go after they died.

atoms.a: Harald was a brave warrior who died fighting in battle.
Erik killed another person in his village and was executed for his crimes.
Ivar was a farmer who died of an illness.

instruction.text: Why did the Vikings value bravery so much?

b.sound: Vikings believed that dying bravely in battle would send them to Valhalla.
Vikings believed that dying bravely in battle would send them to Helheim.

feedback.end: Vikings had strong beliefs about bravery, violence and death, which allowed them to be ruthless in battles.
